# VetReception

> The phone answered every time, triaged to the practice's own protocol, booked into the PIMS.

VetReception answers every call a veterinary practice cannot get to — after hours, during surgery, and at three in the morning — triages it against the practice's own emergency protocol rather than a generic script, books the appointment straight into the PIMS, and leaves the front desk a written summary instead of a voicemail to work through.

## Start here

- [VetReception: 24/7 Vet Call Answering Into Your PIMS](https://vetreception.swades.ai/): VetReception answers every veterinary call, triages against the practice's own written emergency protocol, and books straight into the PIMS.

- [Vet Clinic Missed Calls: What They Cost and How to Stop Them](https://vetreception.swades.ai/the-problem-in-the-words-veterinary-practices-use/): Missed calls at a veterinary practice are not a front-desk failure. Here is what they cost, why they persist, and how calls get answered and booked.
- [Veterinary Practices Pricing: How VetReception Is Priced](https://vetreception.swades.ai/pricing-for-veterinary-practices/): How VetReception pricing works for veterinary practices: what sets the price, what is included, what you pay today for after-hours coverage, and the FAQ.
- [VetReception Integrations: PIMS Booking and Call Summaries](https://vetreception.swades.ai/works-with-the-software-veterinary-practices-already-run/): Which practice management systems VetReception books into, what each connection writes back, how setup runs, and what happens on a clinical call.
